Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Based on Nimbus's Q4 forecast and the spike pattern you shared, I put together a compact renewal proposal that accelerates your hosted monthly commit and adds a short-term soft-cap (soft burst) to cover peak events without changing the SLA baseline. Key bullets: 

- Move from current 1.5M token/mo commit to 3.0M token/mo (effective 2027-01-01)
- 20% discounted rate band for the bumped commit for year 1
- Soft-cap: 30% burst pocket that can be used up to twice/month; usage above soft-cap billed at standard overage rate
- Ops: we’ll enable prefix caching and an optimized batching profile; karthik will provide the throughput tuning notes

I attached the draft renewal and a small throughput table so your SREs can validate assumptions. If this looks good, I’ll route to legal and generate a DocuSign with the new commit and term change.

Hi Alex — quick tech note from the SE side. TL;DR: soft-cap implemented as a calendar-month burst pocket; requests are not abruptly dropped — they are deprioritized and subject to a best-effort queuing policy. Details: 

- Burst accounting: soft-cap is calendar-month based and does not roll over. Unused burst capacity expires at month end. We generally recommend calendar-month to align with billing.
- Runtime behavior: when commit + soft-cap is consumed, traffic hits the standard tenant-level rate limiter. Two safeguards available:
  * Soft-priority queue: best-effort serving with longer tail latencies (used for non-latency-critical batch jobs)
  * Controlled throttling: token-bucket drop policy for strict low-latency endpoints (returns 429 to callers)
- Recommendation: instrument these signals: X-Redwood-Latency-Mode, X-Redwood-Quota-Status (headers we can enable). For user-facing request paths, we recommend the controlled throttling path with a client-side retry/backoff. For internal batch pipelines, use soft-priority queue.
- Ops runbook: if you expect >50% of burst utilization regularly, we should consider raising the commit; auto-burst is not intended as a permanent substitute.

I attached an ops snippet (I pasted it below) and flagged the config knobs we'll set at onboarding time. Happy to hop on a 20-min call with your SREs.

--karthik
Karthik Iyer | Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Runtime: when soft-cap triggers, behavior per karthik: soft-priority queue OR controlled throttling (your choice per endpoint). We'll add the request headers to your SDK wrappers.
